1.word_for_word: षोडशे — in the sixteenth chapter; कालियस्य उक्तः निग्रहः — the subjugation of Kāliya is described; यमुना-ह्रदे — in the pool of the Yamunā; तत्-पत्नीभिः स्तुते — when he had been praised by his wives; अथ कृष्णेन अनुग्रहः कृतः — then Kṛṣṇa bestowed grace upon him; हत्वा रासभ-दैतेयान् — having killed the ass-demons; जग्ध्वा ताल-फलानि अलम् — having eaten the palm fruits to satisfaction; प्रीतः अनृत्यत् — delighted, he danced; फणा-रङ्गे कालियस्य — upon Kāliya's hoods as a stage; कलानिधिः — the repository of arts; उदवासयन् — he drove him out; निःसारितवान् — he expelled him
1.translation: In the sixteenth chapter the subjugation of Kāliya in the pool of the Yamunā is described. Then, after he had been praised by his wives, Kṛṣṇa bestowed grace upon him. Having killed the ass-demons and eaten the palm fruits to satisfaction, the repository of arts, delighted, danced upon Kāliya's hoods as a stage. ‘Udavāsayan’ means ‘he drove him out,’ that is, ‘he expelled him.’

2.word_for_word: बहूनि युगानि आवसः यस्य — whose residence had lasted many yugas; तम् अहिम् — that serpent; स वै अहिः — that very serpent; अजल-चरः अपि — although not a water-dweller; तस्मिन् अन्तर्-जले — in that deep water; यथा येन प्रकारेण आसीत् — how, in what manner, he came to be there; अथवा — or; बहूनि युगानि आवासः यथा भवति — how a residence lasting many yugas came about; तथा येन प्रकारेण स वै तत्र आसीत् — in what manner that serpent was there; कथ्यताम् — let it be told
2.translation: ‘The serpent whose residence had lasted for many yugas’ means that very serpent. Although a serpent is not an aquatic creature, let it be told how, and in what manner, he came to live in that deep water. Or the sense is: let it be told how he came to have a residence there for many yugas, and in what manner that serpent came to be there.

3.word_for_word: गोपालेन — by the cowherd; यत् उदारं चरितम् आचरितम् — whatever exalted deed was performed; तत् एव अमृतम् — that itself is nectar; अतः कथ्यताम् — therefore let it be told
3.translation: Whatever exalted deed was performed by the cowherd is itself nectar. Therefore let it be told.

4.word_for_word: श्रप्यमाणं पच्यमानं पयः यस्य — whose water was, as it were, being heated and cooked; सः — that pool; अतः — therefore; उपरि गच्छन्तः खगाः — birds passing above; यस्मिन् पतन्ति — fall into it
4.translation: The pool was such that its water was, as it were, being heated and cooked. Therefore birds flying above it would fall into it.

5.word_for_word: किं च — moreover; विप्रुष्मता अम्बु-कण-युक्तेन — carrying spray, furnished with droplets of water; विषोद-तरङ्ग-स्पर्शि-मारुतेन — by the wind that touched the waves of the poisoned water; स्पृष्टाः — when touched; यस्य तीरगाः म्रियन्ते — creatures on whose banks died; स ह्रदः आसीत् — such was that pool
5.translation: Moreover, that pool was such that creatures on its banks died merely by being touched by the spray-bearing wind that had come into contact with the waves of its poisoned water.

6.word_for_word: तं कालियम् — that Kāliya; चण्डः वेगः यस्य — whose force was fierce; तत् विषम् एव वीर्यं यस्य — whose very potency was poison; कदम्बम् — the kadamba tree; भाविना श्री-कृष्ण-चरण-स्पर्श-भाग्येन — because of the future fortune of being touched by Śrī Kṛṣṇa's feet; स एकः तत्-तीरे न शुष्कः — that one alone on the bank had not dried up; अमृतम् आहरता गरुत्मता क्रान्तत्वात् — because it had been stepped upon by Garuḍa while he was carrying nectar; इति च पुराणान्तरम् — so another Purāṇa states; आस्फोट्य बाहुम् — slapping his arm; कर-तलेन आहत्य — striking it with the palm; गाढा दृढं बद्धा रशना — whose girdle was firmly and tightly bound; कटि-बन्धन-वस्त्रम् — the cloth tied about the waist
6.translation: ‘That Kāliya’ means Kāliya whose force was fierce and whose very potency was poison. ‘The kadamba’ refers to the kadamba tree. It should be understood that this one tree alone on that bank had not dried up because of the future good fortune of being touched by Śrī Kṛṣṇa's feet. Another Purāṇa says that it remained because Garuḍa had stepped upon it while carrying nectar. ‘Āsphoṭya bāhum’ means slapping his arm with the palm. His raśanā, the cloth tied around his waist, was bound firmly and tightly.

7.word_for_word: तदा सर्पस्य ह्रदः — then the serpent's pool; पुरुष-श्रेष्ठस्य पतन-भारेण — by the weight of the fall of the Supreme Person; सङ्क्षोभितानाम् उरगाणाम् विषैः — by the poisons of the serpents that were agitated; उन्नतः अम्बु-राशिः यस्य — whose mass of water rose up; विषेण कषायी-कृताः भयंकराः ऊर्मयः यस्य — whose terrifying waves had been made acrid by poison; पर्यक् परितः धावन् — rushing out all around; धनुः-शतं प्लुतः प्रसृतः — spread for a hundred bow-lengths; न एतत् चित्रम् — this is not astonishing; अनन्त-बलस्य — because his strength is unlimited
7.translation: Then the serpent's pool had its mass of water raised by the poison of the serpents agitated by the weight of the Supreme Person's fall. Its terrifying waves had been made acrid by poison, and the water rushed out and spread for a hundred bow-lengths all around. This is not astonishing, the text says, because his strength is unlimited.

8.word_for_word: ह्रदे विहरतः — while he was sporting in the pool; भुज-दण्ड-आहत-उदक-घोषम् श्रुत्वा — hearing the roar of the water struck by his staff-like arms; ततः — then; स्व-सदन-अभिभवम् निरीक्ष्य — seeing the invasion of his own dwelling; तत् असहमानः — unable to tolerate it; सर्पः समसरत् समाजगाम — the serpent rushed forth and came to him
8.translation: While Kṛṣṇa was sporting in the pool, the serpent heard the roar of the water struck by his staff-like arms. Then, seeing his own dwelling invaded and unable to tolerate it, the serpent rushed forth and came to him.

9.word_for_word: प्रेक्षणीयः — beautiful to behold; सुकुमारः — very tender; घन-वद् उज्ज्वलः — lustrous like a raincloud; श्रीवत्स-पीत-वसनम् — bearing the Śrīvatsa and a yellow garment; ह्रदे विहरतः — as he sported in the pool; उच्चलत् पीतं वस्त्रम् यस्य — whose yellow garment was fluttering; भुजया भोगेन चच्छाद — with his serpentine body, his coil, he covered him; अवेष्टयत् — he encircled him
9.translation: Kṛṣṇa was beautiful to behold, very tender, and lustrous like a raincloud. As he sported in the pool, he bore the Śrīvatsa and his yellow garment fluttered. Kāliya covered him with his serpentine body—that is, with his coil—and encircled him.

12.word_for_word: भुवि भू-कम्प-आदयः — on earth, earthquakes and the like; दिवि उल्का-पात-आदयः — in the sky, falling meteors and the like; आत्मनि वाम-नेत्र-स्फुरण-आदयः — in one's own body, twitching of the left eye and the like; आसन्नं भयम् शंसितुं शीलं येषाम् — whose nature is to announce approaching danger
12.translation: On earth there were earthquakes and the like; in the sky, falling meteors and the like; and in their own bodies, twitching of the left eye and similar signs. Such omens have the character of announcing an approaching danger.

13-15.word_for_word: तान् आलक्ष्य — having observed those omens; गोकुलाः निर्जग्मुः — the inhabitants of Gokula went out; इति तृतीयेन अन्वयः — this is to be connected with the third verse; भय-उद्विग्नाः — agitated by fear; भय-हेतुभ्यः भीताः — frightened by the causes of fear; भयेन कम्पमानाः इति वा — or, trembling with fear; न तं विदन्ति — they did not know the truth of it; अतद्-विदः — not knowing that; पशु-वृत्तयः — having the ways of simple creatures; अतिवत्सलाः — exceedingly affectionate
13-15.translation: ‘Having observed those omens, the inhabitants of Gokula went out’ is the construction to be completed with the third verse. ‘Agitated by fear’ means frightened by the causes of fear, or trembling with fear. ‘Atad-vidaḥ’ means that they did not know the true situation. ‘Paśu-vṛttayaḥ’ describes them as simple in disposition, and they were exceedingly affectionate.

17.word_for_word: भगवन्तं लक्षयन्ति यानि पदानि — the footprints which mark Bhagavān; तैः पदैः सूचितया — indicated by those footprints; पदवी-मार्गेण — along the track or path
17.translation: They went along the track indicated by those footprints which marked Bhagavān.

18.word_for_word: पदैः मार्ग-ज्ञान-प्रकारम् आह — the verse states how the path was known from the footprints; विश्पतेः श्री-कृष्णस्य — of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the lord of the people; अन्येषां पदानाम् अन्तरान्तरे — among the other footprints at intervals; तत्-तद्-अपोहेन — by excluding each of the others; गवां श्रुतीनां मार्गे — on the path of the cows, figuratively the Vedic revelations; सत्वराः अप्रमत्ताः योगिनः — alert and heedful yogins; तत्-तत्-उपाधि-अपवादेन — by negating each limiting adjunct; यथा परं तत्त्वं मृगयन्ते — just as they seek the supreme reality; तद्वत् — in the same way
18.translation: The verse states how the path was recognized from the footprints. At intervals among the other footprints they identified those of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, the lord of the people, by excluding the others one by one. The sense is that, just as alert and heedful yogins seek the supreme reality on the path of the śrutis by negating one limiting adjunct after another, so the cowherds traced Kṛṣṇa's path by distinguishing his footprints from all the rest.

19.word_for_word: ततः च — then; सर्प-शरीर-वेष्टितं कृष्णम् — Kṛṣṇa encircled by the serpent's body; दूरात् निरीक्ष्य — seeing from afar; गोपान् च पशून् च तथा निरीक्ष्य — and likewise seeing the cowherds and animals; आर्ताः — distressed; परम-कश्मलम् — extreme bewilderment; परं मोहम् प्रापुः — they fell into profound delusion
19.translation: Then, seeing from afar Kṛṣṇa encircled by the serpent's body, and likewise seeing the cowherds and the animals, they became distressed and fell into the deepest bewilderment.

20.word_for_word: प्रियेण श्री-कृष्णेन — by their beloved Śrī Kṛṣṇa; व्यतिहृतं विरहितम् — deprived, bereft; त्रैलोक्यम् — the three worlds; शून्यम् ददृशुः — they saw as empty
20.translation: They saw the three worlds as empty, because they were bereft of their beloved Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

23.word_for_word: अनन्य-गतिम् आत्मानम् इत्थं निरीक्ष्य — seeing himself in this way to be their sole refuge; अत एव आत्म-हेतोः — and therefore, because of himself; स्व-गोकुलम् अतिदुःखितम् आज्ञाय — knowing his own Gokula to be exceedingly distressed; उरङ्ग-बन्धात् उदतिष्ठत् — he rose up from the serpent's bondage
23.translation: Seeing in this way that he himself was their sole refuge, and knowing that his own Gokula had become exceedingly distressed on his account, he rose up from the serpent's coils.

24.word_for_word: तस्य प्रथ्यमानेन वपुषा — as Kṛṣṇa's body expanded; व्यथित-आत्म-शरीरः भुजङ्गः — the serpent's own body became pained; कुण्डलीम् उन्मुच्य — loosening his coil; तं त्यक्त्वा — releasing him; कुपितः — enraged; स्व-फणान् उन्नमय्य — raising his hoods; श्वसन् केवलम् ईक्षमाणः तस्थौ — breathing heavily, he stood simply staring; श्वसन-रन्ध्रेषु नासा-विवरेषु विषं यस्य — with poison in the breathing passages, the nostrils; अम्बरीषवत् सन्तप्तानि स्तब्धानि ईक्षणानि यस्य — whose fixed eyes were blazing like a heated cooking vessel; उल्मुकानि मुखेषु यस्य — whose mouths were like firebrands
24.translation: As Kṛṣṇa's body expanded, the serpent's own body was tormented. Kāliya loosened his coil and released him; then, enraged, he raised his hoods, breathed heavily, and stood staring at him. Poison issued through his breathing passages, his nostrils; his rigid eyes were burning like a heated cooking vessel, and his mouths were like blazing firebrands.

25.word_for_word: हरिः च क्रीडन् — and Hari, playing; तम् अमुं सर्वं परिससार — circled all around him; परितः बभ्राम — moved round about; अति-कराल-विष-अग्नि-युक्ता दृष्टिः यस्य — whose gaze was filled with exceedingly terrible poisonous fire; जिह्वया द्वि-शिखया — with his two-forked tongue; प्रतिमुखम् — facing him
25.translation: Hari, as if playing, moved all around Kāliya and circled him. The serpent's gaze was filled with exceedingly terrible poisonous fire, and his two-forked tongue flickered as he faced Kṛṣṇa.

26.word_for_word: एवं परिभ्रमेण एव हतम् ओजः यस्य — whose strength had been destroyed by being made to circle in this way; उन्नतौ अंसौ यस्य — whose shoulders were raised; तस्य मूर्धसु रत्न-निकराः — the clusters of jewels upon his heads; तेषां स्पर्शेन अत्यरुणं पादाम्बुजम् — Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet became very red by touching them; कथं चञ्चलेषु शिरःसु ननर्त — how did he dance upon moving heads; अखिल-कलानाम् आदि-गुरुः — he is the original teacher of all arts
26.translation: Kāliya's strength had been destroyed simply by Kṛṣṇa's circling him in this way, and his shoulders were raised. By contact with the clusters of jewels on Kāliya's heads, Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet became exceedingly red. One may ask: how could he dance upon heads that were constantly moving? The answer is that he is the original teacher of every art.

27.word_for_word: उपसेदुः — they approached; प्राप्ताः — they came near
27.translation: ‘Upaseduḥ’ means that they approached, that they came near.

28.word_for_word: शतैक-शीर्ष्णः — of the hundred-and-one-headed serpent; शतम् एकानि मुख्यानि शीर्षाणि यस्य — whose hundred principal heads were prominent; क्षीण-आयुषः अपि — although his life was failing; पुनः भ्रमतः — as he kept moving about; यत् यत् शिरः न नमते — whichever head did not bow; स्तब्धतां न जहाति — did not abandon its rigidity; नृत्य-च्छलेन अङ्घ्रि-पातैः — under the guise of dancing, with the falls of his feet; तत् तत् ममर्द — he crushed each such head; आस्यतः मुखेभ्यः — from his mouths; नस्तः नासा-विवरेभ्यः च — and from the nostrils; असृक् वमन् — he vomited blood
28.translation: Kāliya is described as having a hundred and one heads, a hundred of them being principal. Although his life was ebbing, he continued to move about; whichever head would not bow and would not give up its rigid defiance, Kṛṣṇa crushed with the falls of his feet under the guise of dancing. Then Kāliya vomited blood from his mouths and from his nostrils.

29.word_for_word: पुनः अपि रुषा उच्चैः निश्वसतः — as he again breathed violently in anger; यत् यत् समुन्नमति — whatever head he raised; तत् तत् पदाघाते नानुनमयन् — Kṛṣṇa made each one bend down with the blow of his foot; हृष्टैः गन्धर्व-आदिभिः — by delighted Gandharvas and others; पुष्पैः प्रपूजितः — worshiped with flowers; शेषासनः पुराणः पुरुषः इव — like the Ancient Person whose couch is Śeṣa; यशोदा-नन्दनः — the son of Yaśodā; यद् वा — or; गोपैः पुराणः पुमान् इव दृष्टः — the cowherds saw him as if he were the Ancient Person; यद् वा — or; पुष्पैः प्रपूजितः इव प्रसन्नः सन् — or, becoming pleased as though worshiped with flowers; दमयाम्बभूव — he subdued him; हितं कृतवान् — he did what was beneficial
29.translation: Whenever Kāliya again raised a head while breathing violently in anger, Kṛṣṇa forced that very head down with the blow of his foot. At that moment the delighted Gandharvas and others worshiped Yaśodā's son with flowers, as though he were the Ancient Person reclining upon Śeṣa. Alternatively, the sense is that the cowherds saw him as the Ancient Person while the Gandharvas and others worshiped him with flowers. Or, ‘worshiped with flowers’ may indicate that he became gracious and then thoroughly subdued Kāliya—meaning that he acted for Kāliya's benefit.

31.word_for_word: गर्भे जगन्ति यस्य — he in whose womb the worlds rest; तस्य अतिभारेण अवसन्नम् आक्रान्तम् — overcome and pressed down by his immense weight; पार्ष्णिः — the back of the foot, the heel; आद्यम् — the primal one, Śrī Kṛṣṇa; श्लथन्तः विस्रंसमानाः वसन-आदयः यासाम् — whose garments and the like had loosened and were slipping
31.translation: He in whose womb the worlds rest oppressed Kāliya with his immense weight. ‘Pārṣṇi’ means the back of the foot, the heel. ‘Ādyam’ means the primal one, Śrī Kṛṣṇa. The serpent-wives are described as having their garments and the like loosened and slipping from them.

32.word_for_word: ताः शरणं प्रपन्नाः सत्यः — those women, taking refuge; तं प्रणेमुः — bowed to him; सुविग्न-मनसः — with greatly agitated minds; अतिविह्वल-चित्ताः — their hearts utterly distraught; भुवि — on the ground, either beneath the water or on the bank; शमलस्य पापात्मनः अपि भर्तुः मोक्षेप्सवः — desiring the release even of their sinful husband; भर्तुः यत् शमलम् तस्य वा — or, the release from their husband's sin; भूत-पतिम् — the lord of every living being; शरण-दम् — the giver of shelter
32.translation: Those women took refuge in Kṛṣṇa and bowed to him. Their minds were greatly agitated and their hearts utterly distraught. ‘On the ground’ may mean there beneath the water or on the bank. They desired the deliverance even of their sinful husband—or deliverance from the sin belonging to their husband. They bowed to the Lord of every living being, the giver of shelter.

33.word_for_word: प्रथमं तावत् — first of all; कुपितं भगवन्तम् — the angered Bhagavān; दण्ड-अनुमोदनेन उपशमयन्त्यः — calming him by approving the punishment; स्तुवन्ति — they praise him; दण्डानुमोदनं षड्भिः — approval of the punishment is in six verses; दशभिः च हरेः नतिः — obeisance to Hari in ten; प्रार्थनं पञ्चभिः श्लोकैः — prayer in five verses; न च निग्रह-अनुग्रह-लक्षणं वैषम्यं तव अस्ति — there is no partiality in you in the form of punishment and favor; धत्से दमम् — you impose discipline; अनुशंसन् — considering, examining; आलोचयन् — reflecting upon
33.translation: First, seeking to pacify the angered Bhagavān by approving his punishment, the serpent-wives praise him with the verse beginning ‘nyāyyo hi.’ Their prayer is arranged as follows: six verses approve the punishment, ten offer obeisance to Hari, and five make their request. They say that there is no partiality in him in the form of punishment toward one and favor toward another. ‘You impose discipline’ means that he does so after considering and examining the case.

34.word_for_word: निग्रहः अपि अनुग्रहाय — even punishment is for the sake of grace; इदानीम् अनुग्रहः एव अयम् न निग्रहः — now they say this is grace itself, not punishment; नो — for us, in our view; अमुष्य सर्पत्वं दृश्यते — his condition of being a serpent is evident; तत्-मूल-पाप-निवर्तकः दण्डः — punishment that removes the sin at its root; अनुग्रहः एव — is itself favor; क्रोधत्वेन प्रतीयमानः अपि — even though it appears as anger
34.translation: They had said, ‘Even punishment is for the sake of grace.’ Now they say that this is grace itself and not punishment: ‘It is favor.’ Since his very condition of being a serpent is visible, the punishment that removes the sin lying at the root of that condition is itself an act of grace, even though it appears in the form of anger.

35.word_for_word: महान् च अयम् अनुग्रहः — and this is a very great favor; तस्य पूर्व-पुण्यम् अभिनन्दन्ति — they celebrate whatever former merit he possessed; तपः इति — with the verse beginning 'tapas'; स्वयं मान-रहितेन — by one devoid of self-conceit; अन्येभ्यः मानदेन च — and one who gives honor to others; सर्वं जीवयति — he gives life to all; सर्व-जीवः — the life-giver of all
35.translation: Because this is an exceedingly great favor, they celebrate whatever former merit Kāliya may have possessed with the verse beginning ‘tapas.’ The description is of one who is himself free of pride and who gives honor to others. ‘Sarva-jīva’ means he who gives life to all.

36.word_for_word: न तप-आदि-निमित्तः एष भाग्य-उदयः — this rise of fortune was not caused by austerity and the like; अचिन्त्यं तव कृपा-वैभवम् — it is the inconceivable greatness of your grace; श्लोक-त्रयेण — in three verses; कस्य अनुभावः इति — beginning 'kasya anubhāvaḥ'; ब्रह्म-आदयः अपि — even Brahmā and others; यस्याः श्रियः प्रसादम् इच्छन्ति — desire the favor of that Śrī, Lakṣmī; सा श्रीः ललना — that lady Śrī; त्वत्-अङ्घ्रि-स्पर्श-अधिकारस्य वाञ्छया — desiring eligibility to touch your feet; तपः आचरत् — performed austerity; अस्य सर्पस्य स किं-कृतः — what did this serpent do; को वेत्ति — who knows
36.translation: In three verses beginning ‘kasya anubhāvaḥ’ they say that this rise of fortune was not produced by austerity or any similar cause; it is the inconceivable greatness of your grace. Even Brahmā and others seek through austerity the favor of Śrī, Lakṣmī, yet that supreme lady herself performed austerity out of a desire to gain the privilege of touching your feet. Who, then, knows what this serpent did to obtain such fortune?

37.word_for_word: यत् तव पाद-रजः प्रपन्नाः — those who have attained the dust of your feet; पारमेष्ठ्य-आदि अपि — even the position of Brahmā and the like; तुच्छं मन्यन्ते — regard as insignificant
37.translation: Those who have attained the dust of your feet regard even the position of Brahmā and the like as insignificant.

38.word_for_word: अहो — astonishingly; तत् एषः अयत्नतः एव प्राप — this serpent obtained it without effort; अन्यैः अपि — though it is sought by others as well; कथं-भूतं पाद-रजः — what kind of foot-dust is it; यत् इच्छतः — for one who desires it; सेव्यं मे भवतु इति प्रार्थयमानस्य — praying, 'may it become mine to serve'; समक्षः प्रत्यक्षः एव — directly, visibly before him; विभवः अपेक्षिता संपत् भवति — the desired attainment becomes present
38.translation: Astonishingly, this serpent obtained that foot-dust without effort, though it is sought by others as well. What sort of foot-dust is this? For one who longs for it and prays, ‘May it become mine to serve,’ the desired attainment itself stands directly before him.

39.word_for_word: नमः तुभ्यं भगवते — obeisance to you, Bhagavān; अचिन्त्य-ऐश्वर्य-आदि-गुणाय — endowed with inconceivable lordship and other qualities; दशभिः श्लोकैः विशेषणानि — the epithets are given in ten verses; पुरुषाय — to the Puruṣa; पूर्षु अन्तर्यामि-रूपेण वर्तमानाय — existing within embodied beings as the inner controller; महात्मने — to the great Self; न अति-परिच्छिन्नाय — not narrowly limited; भूतावासाय — the abode or support of the elements and beings; आकाश-आदि-आश्रयाय — the support of ether and the rest; भूताय — to him who already existed; पराय कारणाय — to the transcendent cause; परमात्मने — to the Supreme Self, beyond the cause
39.translation: ‘Obeisance to you, Bhagavān’ means to him who possesses inconceivable lordship and the other divine qualities. To establish this, the wives employ a series of epithets in ten verses. ‘To the Puruṣa’ means to him who exists within embodied beings as the inner controller. ‘To the Mahātman’ indicates that even so he is not narrowly delimited. Why? Because he is ‘the abode of beings and elements,’ the support of ether and the rest. And why is this so? Because he is ‘bhūta,’ the one who existed even before them; ‘para,’ the transcendent cause; and ‘Paramātman,’ the Supreme Self who is beyond even the causal order.

40.word_for_word: कारणत्वं कारणातीतत्वं च समर्थयितुम् — to establish both causality and transcendence of causality; ज्ञान-विज्ञान-निधये — to the repository of jñāna and vijñāna; ज्ञानं ज्ञप्तिः — jñāna is cognition; विज्ञानं चित्-शक्तिः — vijñāna is the power of consciousness; उभयोर् निधये — to the fullness or treasury of both; ब्रह्मणे अनन्त-शक्तये — to Brahman of unlimited power; अगुणाय अविकाराय — without material qualities and without change; प्राकृताय प्रकृति-प्रवर्तकाय — as 'prākṛta,' the mover of prakṛti; अप्राकृताय इति वा — or the reading means 'non-material'; अगुणत्वात् अविकारं ब्रह्म — because it is guṇa-less, Brahman is changeless; ज्ञप्ति-मात्रत्वात् कारणातीतम् — because it is pure cognition, it transcends causality; प्रकृति-प्रवर्तकः अनन्त-शक्तिः ईश्वरः कारणम् — the Lord, of infinite power and mover of prakṛti, is the cause; तद् उभयात्मने नमः — obeisance to him whose nature comprises both aspects
40.translation: To establish both his being the cause and his transcendence of causality, they say, ‘to the repository of jñāna and vijñāna.’ Here jñāna is cognition, while vijñāna is the power of consciousness; he is the treasury, the fullness, of both. Hence he is called Brahman of unlimited power. As Brahman he is without material qualities and without change; he is of unlimited power. ‘Prākṛta’ may mean the one who sets prakṛti in motion, or the reading may be understood as ‘aprākṛta,’ non-material and possessed of unlimited non-material potency. The sense is this: because he is without guṇas, Brahman is changeless; because he is pure cognition, he stands beyond causality; yet as the Lord of infinite power, the mover of prakṛti and repository of conscious potency, he is also the cause. Obeisance to him who possesses both aspects.

41.word_for_word: अनन्त-शक्तित्वात् — because he has unlimited power; काल-शक्त्या विश्व-स्रष्टृत्व-आदि-रूपेण — through the power of time, as creator and so forth of the universe; कालाय — to Time itself; काल-नाभाय — to the support or hub of the power of time; काल-अवयवानां सृष्टि-आदि-समयानां साक्षिणे — witness of the divisions of time, such as the times of creation; विश्वाय विश्व-रूपाय — to the universe, whose form is the universe; तद्-उपद्रष्ट्रे — to its overseer; तत् कर्त्रे — to its maker; विश्व-हेतवे — to the cause of the universe; सर्व-कारक-रूपाय — whose form includes all causal agencies
41.translation: Because his power is unlimited, they bow to him in the form of the creator and so forth of the universe through the power of time: to Time itself; to the ‘navel’ or support of the power of time; and to the witness of the parts of time, such as the moments of creation and dissolution. Thus they bow to him as the universe, whose form is the universe. Does that make him inert? No: he is its overseer. Nor is he merely an observer: he is its maker. Nor merely a maker: he is the cause of the universe, whose nature encompasses all causal agencies.

42.word_for_word: भूत-मात्र-इन्द्रिय-प्राण-मनो-बुद्धि-आशय-आत्मने — whose nature is the elements, subtle elements, senses, vital force, mind, intellect and citta; आशयः चित्तम् — āśaya means citta; भूत-आदि-रूपाय — taking the form of the elements and the rest; सर्व-कारक-रूपाय — whose form comprises all causal factors; अहङ्कार-आत्मतया — in the form of ahaṅkāra; त्रि-गुणेन — through the three guṇas; स्वांश-भूतानाम् आत्मनां जीवानाम् अनुभूतिः गूढा येन — by whom the awareness of the jīvas, who are his own portions, is concealed
42.translation: They further address him as the Self of the elements and subtle elements, the senses, vital force, mind, intellect and āśaya—here āśaya means citta. Thus he takes the form of the elements and all the rest and so has the form of all causal factors. They also bow to him in the form of ahaṅkāra: through the three guṇas, in the created effect, the awareness of the individual selves—the jīvas who are portions of him—is concealed.

43.word_for_word: त्वं तु अहङ्कार-अनावृतः — you, however, are not covered by ahaṅkāra; नमः अनन्ताय — obeisance to the infinite; अहङ्कार-अपरिच्छेदात् — because ahaṅkāra does not delimit him; सूक्ष्माय — to the subtle, because unseen; कूटस्थाय — to the immutable; उपाधि-कृत-विकार-अभावात् — because changes produced by limiting adjuncts do not affect him; विपश्चिते — to the all-knowing one; नाना-वाद-अनुरोधाय — who accommodates diverse doctrines; अस्ति नास्ति सर्वज्ञः किञ्चिज्ज्ञः बद्धः मुक्तः एकः अनेकः — 'he exists, does not exist, is omniscient, knows only a little, is bound, liberated, one, many'; मायया अनुवर्तते — he appears to conform to them through māyā; वाच्य-वाचक-शक्तये — to the power of the signified and the signifier; अभिधान-अभिधेय-शक्ति-भेदात् — because of the distinction between word and referent; नानात्वेन प्रतीयमानाय — appearing as manifold
43.translation: They praise him as one who, unlike the jīva, is not covered by ahaṅkāra: ‘obeisance to the Infinite,’ because ahaṅkāra cannot delimit him; ‘to the subtle,’ because he is unseen; ‘to the immutable,’ because no modification produced by limiting adjuncts affects him; and ‘to the all-knowing.’ Having praised him as he truly is, they praise the inconceivability of his māyā in the phrase ‘one who accommodates diverse doctrines.’ Through māyā he appears to conform to the many claims—‘he exists,’ ‘he does not exist,’ ‘he is omniscient,’ ‘he knows only a little,’ ‘he is bound,’ ‘he is liberated,’ ‘he is one,’ ‘he is many,’ and so on. He is also the power of the signified and of the signifier: through the distinction of the powers of word and referent he appears as manifold.

44.word_for_word: अनावृतत्वम् — his being unobscured; नमः प्रमाण-मूलाय — obeisance to the root of the means of knowledge; चक्षुर्-आदीनां चक्षुर्-आदि-रूपाय — the eye of the eye and corresponding ground of the other senses; कवये — to the seer; स्वयं तत्-निरपेक्ष-ज्ञानाय — whose knowledge is self-sufficient and independent of those instruments; शास्त्र-योनये — to the source of scripture; वेदात्मक-निःश्वासाय — whose exhalation is the Veda; प्रवृत्ताय निवृत्ताय निगमाय — to the Veda teaching action and cessation
44.translation: They indicate his unobscured nature from another angle: obeisance to the root of all means of knowledge, to him who is, as it were, the eye of the eye and likewise the ground of the other senses. Therefore he is ‘kavi,’ the seer whose knowledge is self-sufficient and independent of those instruments. Why? Because he is the source of scripture, whose very exhalation is the Veda. Obeisance again and again to the Veda in its teachings of both engagement and withdrawal.

45.word_for_word: अनावृत-ऐश्वर्यत्वात् — because his lordship is unobscured; चतुर्-मूर्ति-रूपेण — in the form of the four manifestations; सर्व-उपास्यत्वेन — as worshipable by all; नमः कृष्णाय — obeisance to Kṛṣṇa; रामाय सङ्कर्षणाय — to Rāma, Saṅkarṣaṇa; वसुदेव-सुताय — to the son of Vasudeva; वसुदेव-शब्दितं शुद्धं सत्त्वम् — pure sattva called 'vasudeva'; तत्र प्रकाशमानाय वासुदेवाय — to Vāsudeva manifest therein; सात्वताम् उपासकानां पतये — to the lord of the Sātvata worshipers; सालोक्य-आदिना पालकाय — who protects/rewards them with sālokya and the like; चतुर्-मूर्तये कृष्णाय — to Kṛṣṇa in the fourfold manifestation
45.translation: Because his lordship is unobscured, they bow to him as the fourfold manifestation worshiped by all, in the verse beginning ‘obeisance to Kṛṣṇa.’ ‘To Rāma’ means to Saṅkarṣaṇa. He is the son of Vasudeva; and ‘Vāsudeva’ also means the one who shines in pure sattva, which is called vasudeva. He is the lord of the Sātvatas, his worshipers, protecting or rewarding them through sālokya and the other forms of divine attainment. Thus: obeisance to you, Kṛṣṇa, in the fourfold manifestation.

46.word_for_word: कथं चतुर्-मूर्तिता — how is there a fourfold manifestation; गुण-प्रदीपाय — to him who illuminates the guṇas, here the inner faculties; गुणाः अन्तः-करणानि — the guṇas are the inner instruments; तानि प्रदीपयति — he illuminates them; चित्त-आदि-अधिष्ठातृत्वेन — by presiding over citta and the rest; चतुर्-मूर्तिता — hence the fourfold manifestation; एकस्य एव कथं चतुष्ट्वम् — how can the one be four; गुणात्म-च्छादनाय — concealing himself by those very faculties/qualities; उपासकानां फल-वैचित्र्याय — for the diversity of results obtained by worshipers; नानात्वेन प्रकाशमानाय — manifesting as manifold; गुण-वृत्ति-उपलक्ष्याय — recognizable through the functions of the inner faculties; गुण-द्रष्ट्रे — to the witness of those guṇas; स्व-संविदे — self-cognizing; अगोचराय — not an object of cognition
46.translation: How is he fourfold? They answer with ‘obeisance to the illuminator of the guṇas.’ Here the guṇas are the inner faculties; he illuminates them. Because he presides over citta and the other inner faculties, he is spoken of as fourfold. But how can the one become four? They answer: he conceals himself through those very guṇas and manifests as manifold so that his worshipers may receive diverse results. How, then, is he perceived? He is ‘indicated by the functions of the guṇas’: he is recognized through functions such as consciousness and ascertainment in citta and the other faculties. This is further explained by ‘the seer of the guṇas,’ their witness. Yet he can only be indicated in this way, not grasped as an object; hence he is ‘self-cognizing,’ beyond the range of objectifying knowledge.

47.word_for_word: अगोचरत्वम् उपलक्ष्यत्वं च — his being beyond objectification yet indicable; अव्याकृत-विहाराय — whose play is unmanifest, of unfathomable greatness; अतर्क्य-महिम्ने — whose greatness cannot be reasoned out; सर्व-व्याकृत-सिद्धये — through whom all manifested effects come to be and become known; हृषीकेश — O Hṛṣīkeśa; करण-प्रवर्तक — mover of the senses; किं विषय-ईप्सया — is it from a desire for objects; न — no; मुनये आत्मारामाय — to the sage who delights in himself; किं साधन-वशेन वा — is it due to dependence on some means; न हि — certainly not; मौन-शीलिने — whose nature is silence; मौनम् आत्मारामता तत्-स्वभावाय — whose very nature is the stillness of self-delight
47.translation: Showing both that he is beyond objectification and that he can nevertheless be indicated, they bow to him as ‘one whose play is unmanifest,’ that is, whose greatness is beyond reasoning, and as the one through whom all manifested effects arise and become evident. Another indication is: ‘O Hṛṣīkeśa, mover of the senses.’ Does he move them because he desires sense objects? No—he is the muni, one who delights in himself. Is even that state dependent on some discipline or means? No: he is naturally established in silence; that silence, the state of delighting in himself, is his very nature.

48.word_for_word: परावर-गति-ज्ञाय — knower of the courses of the higher and lower, gross and subtle; क्वापि न सज्जमानाय — attached nowhere; सर्वाध्यक्षाय — overlord of all; सर्वस्य अधिष्ठात्रे — substratum and ruler of everything; अविश्वाय — beyond the world, the limit reached by negating it; विश्वाय — to the universe, the substratum of its apparent transformation; तत्-द्रष्ट्रे — witness of it; अध्यास-अपवाद-साक्षिणे — witness of superimposition and its sublation; अविद्या-विद्याभ्यां हेतवे — cause, through ignorance and knowledge, of superimposition and sublation; यद् वा — alternatively; विश्व-तैजस-आदि-अवस्था-रहिताय — free from the states called Viśva, Taijasa and so on; मायया स्वांशैः तत्-तत्-अवस्थाय — through māyā and his own portions assuming those states; भाव-अभाव-साक्षिणे — witness of the presence and absence of those states; निरतिशय-ऐश्वर्याय — possessed of unsurpassed lordship; विशेषणैः असङ्कीर्णैः — with distinct, unmixed epithets; अहि-स्त्रीभिः प्रसन्नः — pleased by the serpent-wives; तासाम् इव भवेत् हरिः — may Hari be toward you as he was toward them
48.translation: Why is this so? He knows the courses of the higher and lower, the gross and subtle, and is therefore attached nowhere. He is the overlord and substratum of all. He is ‘aviśva,’ beyond the world, the terminus reached when the world is negated; and he is also ‘viśva,’ the substratum upon which the world appears as a transformation. He is its witness, the witness both of superimposition and of its sublation, and through ignorance and knowledge respectively he is the causal ground of those two. Alternatively, ‘aviśva’ means that he is free from the states called Viśva, Taijasa and so forth, while ‘viśva’ means that through māyā and his own portions he assumes the respective states; yet he remains the witness of their presence and absence. Thus, by his knowledge of every course, his being the substratum of all, his self-delight and the other unsurpassed powers, obeisance is offered to him. The concluding benediction says in substance: may Hari, pleased by the serpent-wives through these distinct epithets, be pleased with you as he was with them.

49.word_for_word: दण्ड-अनुमोदनेन नमस्कारैः च भगवन्तं प्रसाद्य — having propitiated Bhagavān by approving the punishment and by obeisances; त्वद्-अधीनानां प्राणिनां कः अपराधः — what offense is there in creatures dependent upon you; त्वं हि — you indeed; अस्य लोकस्य जन्म-आदि त्वम् एव अकृतः अकरोः — you yourself brought about the birth and other processes of this world; संस्कार-रूपेण सतः स्वभावान् — their existing dispositions in the form of latent impressions; घोरत्व-आदीन् प्रतिबोधयन् — awakening ferocity and the rest; ईहसे क्रीडसि — you act, you play; यद् वा — or; अस्य जन्म-आदीन् त्वम् ईहसे — you undertake its birth and the rest; अनादिः काल-शक्तिः तां धारयति — he bears the beginningless power of time
49.translation: Having propitiated Bhagavān by approving his punishment and by offering obeisances, they now pray with this thought: ‘What independent offense can there be in creatures who are dependent upon you?’ ‘You indeed’ brought about the birth and other processes of this world that previously had not arisen; then, awakening the respective dispositions already present as latent impressions—ferocity and the like—you act, you play. Or the construction may be: you yourself undertake the birth and the other processes of this world. The accompanying epithet means that you bear the beginningless power of time.

50.word_for_word: अतः तस्य तव एव अमूः तनवः तन्यन्ते — therefore these bodies are extended from you alone; क्रीडा-उपस्कराः — implements of your play; तथापि — nevertheless; तव अधुना शान्ताः प्रियाः — now the peaceful are dear to you; सतां धर्म-परिपालन-इच्छया — from a desire to preserve the dharma of the good; ईहतः प्रवर्तमानस्य — as you act and engage; तान् अवितुं स्थातुः — as you remain here to protect them
50.translation: Therefore these bodies are extended from you alone and are implements of your play. Nevertheless, at present the peaceful are dear to you, because you act from a desire to preserve the dharma of the good and remain here in order to protect them.

51.word_for_word: एवं — thus; तव अप्रिय-आचरण-आदि-अपराधः — the offense consisting in conduct displeasing to you and the like; तर्हि सोढव्यः — should therefore be tolerated or forgiven
51.translation: Thus the offense consisting in conduct displeasing to you and the like should therefore be tolerated—forgiven.

53.word_for_word: युष्मद्-अनुग्रहे अन्येषां मृत्युः एव इति चेत् — if it be objected that favor to you would mean death for others; तत् न — not so; विधेहि इति — therefore they say 'ordain'; त्वद्-आज्ञया — by your command; प्राणिनः न अद्याम — we shall not eat living creatures; इति भावः — this is the sense
53.translation: If it be objected, ‘If you show favor to them, that will simply mean death for other creatures,’ the wives reply that it need not be so, and therefore say, ‘Ordain for us.’ The sense is: ‘By your command we shall not eat living creatures.’

56.word_for_word: यत् असद्-ग्रहः — because it consists in grasping what is unreal; यतः स्वभावः असद्-ग्रह-रूपः — because one's nature takes the form of attachment to the unreal; यद् वा — or; यतः स्वभावात् — from that innate disposition; असति देह-आदौ ग्रहः — attachment to the unreal body and the like; सः दुस्त्यजः — that attachment is difficult to abandon
56.translation: ‘Because it is an attachment to the unreal’ means that one's ingrained nature takes the form of grasping what is unreal. Or the sense is: because of that innate disposition, one's attachment to unreal things such as the body is exceedingly difficult to abandon.

57.word_for_word: गुणैः विविधतया सृज्यते — it is created in diverse ways by the guṇas; इति गुण-विसर्जनम् — therefore it is called a manifestation of the guṇas; तत्र अपि — even within it; नाना-स्वभाव-आदयः यस्य — it possesses diverse natures and the other listed differences
57.translation: It is called ‘guṇa-visarjanam’ because it is brought forth in diverse forms by the guṇas. And even within that creation there are the various dispositions and the other differences enumerated in the verse.

58.word_for_word: जात्या जन्मना एव — by our very species, by birth itself; उरुः मन्युः येषाम् — we whose anger is great; ते वयम् — such are we; स्वयं कथं त्यजामः — how could we abandon it by ourselves
58.translation: We are of a species whose anger is great from birth itself. How, then, could we abandon that nature by ourselves?

59.word_for_word: हि यस्मात् — because indeed; तत्र त्वत्-माया-त्यागे — in the matter of giving up your māyā; भवान् एव कारणम् — you alone are the cause; अनुग्रहं विधेहि — therefore bestow favor; ईश्वरत्वात् निग्रहं वा विधेहि — or, because you are the Lord, impose punishment; यत् मन्यसे तत् विधेहि — do whatever you deem fit; ममाज्ञया खादन्ति इति — the electronic reading contains this intervening phrase, whose wording is textually unclear in context
59.translation: Because you alone are the cause in the matter of our giving up your māyā, bestow your favor upon us—or, because you are the Lord, impose punishment. Do whichever you consider fitting. The electronic text here also contains the phrase ‘mamājñayā khādantīti’; its wording is unclear in this context, so it is retained rather than silently rewritten.

60.word_for_word: यतः — because; गोभिः नृभिः च — by cows and by people; नदी भुज्यते — the river is to be used and enjoyed
60.translation: The reason is that the river is to be used by the cows and by human beings.

61.word_for_word: न युष्मत्तः भयम् आप्नुयात् — no one should incur fear from you; तस्य युष्माभिः भयम् न उत्पादनीयम् — you are not to produce fear in such a person; इति आज्ञा — this is the command
61.translation: The command is that no one should incur fear from you; you are not to create fear in such a person.

62.word_for_word: इतः अपि त्वया निर्गन्तव्यम् — for this reason too you must leave this place; यो अस्मिन् इति — this is expressed by the verse beginning 'yo 'smin'; त्वयि स्थिते तत् न सम्भवति — while you remain here, that cannot be possible
62.translation: For this reason also, you must leave this place; this is stated by the verse beginning ‘yo 'smin.’ While you remain here, the intended condition cannot be maintained.

63.word_for_word: न च तव गरुड-भयं भवेत् — and you will have no fear of Garuḍa; द्वीपम् इति — this is indicated by the word 'island' in the verse
63.translation: Nor will you have any fear of Garuḍa; this is the point introduced by the reference to the island in the verse.
